AdminModelInput.description:
A whole model, as the edit form submits it (``POST``/``PUT``).

Field-for-field ``models.yaml``'s ``ModelEntry`` with two differences:
``family_key`` names a row in ``/admin/model-families`` (the display name
comes from there), and ``credential_ref`` may name an admin-entered
provider credential instead of ``api_key_env`` -- never both.
AdminModelInput.title: AdminModelInput

AdminModelPatch.description:
Quick toggles from the list view. Absent fields are left unchanged;
an explicit ``null`` for ``family_key``/``display_order`` clears it.
AdminModelPatch.title: AdminModelPatch

AdminRunRecord.description:
The public :class:`RunRecord` plus the admin-only provenance columns.

A subclass rather than new fields on ``RunRecord`` so the PUBLIC ``/runs``
payload stays byte-identical.
AdminRunRecord.title: AdminRunRecord

AuthEventInput.description:
Posted by the frontend's Auth.js ``events`` -- the only record of a
DENIED sign-in, since a non-member never reaches any other route.
AuthEventInput.title: AuthEventInput

CostRates.description: USD per *million* tokens.  Zero for self-hosted models.
CostRates.title: CostRates

Credential.description: A stored provider key's METADATA. No key material in any form.
Credential.title: Credential

CriterionScore.description:
One rubric criterion's contribution to a judged :class:`Score`.

Exists so that a four-criterion rubric is not collapsed into a single float
before anyone can read it.  "specificity 0.4, tone 0.9" is precisely what a
professor reviewing a recommendation wants to see; "0.58" is not.

Populated by :class:`ida_harness.judge.LLMJudge`; empty for programmatic
scorers.  :attr:`value` is the criterion's score **normalised onto [0, 1]**
from the rubric's scale, and :attr:`weight` is copied from the rubric, so
the weighted total on the parent :class:`Score` is reconstructible from
these rows alone -- which is what makes a judge-calibration study a query
rather than a re-run.
CriterionScore.title: CriterionScore

FamiliesInput.description: The focused "assign families" body, for a class or a unit.
FamiliesInput.title: FamiliesInput

Issue.description:
One validation finding.  ``path`` is what the UI pins the message to.

Paths are the validators' own (``samples[3].target``, ``serving.model_id``)
or ``line N, col M`` for a YAML parse error.
Issue.title: Issue

Quantization.description: Weight precision as served.  ``unknown`` is honest for hosted APIs.
Quantization.title: Quantization

ResultRecord.description:
**One scored sample.**  The durable unit the UI and the recommender read.

Every field needed to reproduce and to *cite* the number is present on the
record itself (D-1, and D-3's evidence-traceability requirement): serving
config by value, task git SHA, transcript pointer, token + cost accounting.
ResultRecord.title: ResultRecord

RunLaunchInput.description:
What to measure. ``family_keys`` expands to each family's live tasks and
is unioned with ``task_ids``; at least one of the two must name something.
RunLaunchInput.title: RunLaunchInput

RunRecord.description:
A run: one (task, model) pair's worth of work, plus its rollup.

A ``RunRequest`` covering 3 tasks x 2 models produces **6** ``RunRecord``s.
Keeping the grain at (task, model) means a slow model cannot block the
display of a fast one, and a partial failure is isolated.
RunRecord.title: RunRecord

RunStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a :class:`RunRecord`.

``queued`` -> ``running`` -> (``succeeded`` | ``partial`` | ``failed`` |
``cancelled``).  ``queued`` may also go straight to ``cancelled``.
A run whose runner dies before finishing does **not** stay ``running``: its
queue claim is recovered and the row goes back to ``queued`` for another
attempt, or -- once attempts are spent, or if no claim survives at all --
it is closed out ``failed`` with a reason.  See
:class:`ida_runner.reaper.Reaper`.  ``running`` therefore means a runner is
genuinely working on it, which is what makes the status worth showing.

The three terminal states are decided by :attr:`RunRecord.error_count`
against :attr:`RunRecord.sample_count` and are **not** interchangeable.
Reporting a run in which every sample errored as ``succeeded`` -- which an
earlier revision did -- tells the reader the model was measured when it was
not, and is exactly the kind of false statement this platform exists to
avoid.  :func:`terminal_status` is the single place that decision is made.
RunStatus.title: RunStatus

SamplingParams.description:
Decoding parameters sent to the endpoint, recorded verbatim on results.

Defaults are the *benchmark* defaults, not the provider defaults: we want
near-deterministic output so that re-running a task reproduces a number.
SamplingParams.title: SamplingParams

Score.description:
A scorer's verdict on one sample.

``value`` is always in ``[0, 1]`` so that scores from different scorers
aggregate.
Score.title: Score

ScorerKind.description: Identifiers of the scorers the harness knows how to construct.
ScorerKind.title: ScorerKind

ServingConfig.description:
The complete, self-contained description of *what answered the prompt*.

This is the D-1 payload.  It is embedded in every :class:`ResultRecord` by
value.  If you add a field here you must also add it to the ``results``
table's ``serving_config`` JSON blob -- which happens automatically,
because that column stores this model's ``model_dump()``.
ServingConfig.title: ServingConfig

ServingStack.description:
*How* an endpoint is served.  Part of the reproducibility record.

Per **D-1** every model -- hosted API, campus vLLM, laptop llama.cpp -- is
reached through the same OpenAI-compatible surface.  This field records
which implementation actually answered, because identical weights served by
different stacks do not produce identical numbers.
ServingStack.title: ServingStack

SystemInfo.description: ``GET /admin/system``: what this deployment is configured to do.
SystemInfo.title: SystemInfo

TaskFamilyUpdate.description: The key is immutable: task ids embed it.
TaskFamilyUpdate.title: TaskFamilyUpdate

TaskValidateInput.description: Exactly one of ``document`` (the form) or ``yaml`` (the YAML tab).
TaskValidateInput.title: TaskValidateInput

TokenUsage.title: TokenUsage
